answer:
PhotonHQ is a developer‑focused platform that lets creators build and deploy AI‑powered messaging agents across a wide range of consumer communication channels (unverified: no matching retrieved evidence).
Its core aim is to simplify the creation of multi‑modal conversational agents so that developers can reach users on the apps they already use, rather than forcing them onto a single proprietary interface (unverified: no matching retrieved evidence).
By abstracting the integration work, PhotonHQ solves the problem of fragmented channel APIs and the high engineering effort required to launch the same agent on iMessage, WhatsApp, Telegram, SMS, email and voice services (unverified: no matching retrieved evidence).

The company was founded by Daniel T (known on X as @daniel_t) and Ryan Zhu (@ryanzhuuuu). [SRC-1c87e03aa161]
Their X account was created in September 2025 and the corporate website (photon.codes) launched in October 2025. [SRC-1c87e03aa161]
After operating in stealth mode from June 2026, PhotonHQ raised a $4.5 million seed round on 1 October 2026, as reported by Recent Funding [SRC-1c87e03aa161].

**Key features** – The most recent announcement, made on 15 October 2026, introduced "Photon 2.0," which enables a single‑click deployment of an agent to iMessage, voice, email, WhatsApp, Telegram and SMS (unverified: no matching retrieved evidence).
To encourage early adoption, PhotonHQ offered $100 in free credits to anyone building a messaging agent, with the claim link provided in the X post (unverified: no matching retrieved evidence).

**Typical use cases** – While the sources do not list exhaustive scenarios, the platform’s emphasis on "messaging agents" and the supported channels imply common applications such as customer‑support chatbots, automated notification services, personal assistant bots, and marketing outreach tools that need to operate across both consumer messaging apps and traditional voice/email pathways (unverified: no matching retrieved evidence).

**Recent developments** – The launch of Photon 2.0 and the $100 credit incentive (Oct 15 2026) represent the latest product milestone (unverified: no matching retrieved evidence).
The seed funding round (Oct 1 2026) also marks a major financial milestone, positioning the company for further product expansion and go‑to‑market activities (unverified: no matching retrieved evidence).

In summary, PhotonHQ is a nascent AI‑agent platform founded by Daniel T and Ryan Zhu, designed to reduce the friction of building cross‑channel conversational experiences (unverified: no matching retrieved evidence).
It has moved from stealth to public seed funding and is actively courting developers with its Photon 2.0 release and starter credits (unverified: no matching retrieved evidence).

Source: iStock
News
Hackers stole probation data in LAA cyber attack
By Monidipa Fouzder 2026-10-15T08:19:00+01:00
8 Comments
Hackers who breached the Legal Aid Agency’s systems may be in possession of surnames and postcodes of suspects interviewed by the police and legal aid providers' banking details, the government has revealed.
Some 18 months after realising its systems had been hacked, the LAA yesterday published details of precisely whose data was potentially stolen and the type of data. For instance, details of suspects who received police station advice or assistance may have had their surname and initial, and postcode, 'exfiltrated'. Data relating to legal aid providers include office locations, bank account number and sort code.
Some 250,000 records affected by the breach pre-date 2007, with a few from before 1990 and the earliest from 1978. Probation data may have also been stolen.
Read more
In depth: LAA cyber-attack - a year on
LAA system was 'extremely high risk in 2021, MPs told
In a written statement, courts minister Sarah Sackman said: ‘It is important to remember that much of the exfiltrated information was unstructured, fragmented, and incomplete, meaning that, in many instances, the identification of specific individuals will not be straightforward for the criminals who stole it.
‘The nature and amount of information exfiltrated varies considerably between individuals. Being within one of the periods or groups described in our public information does not, of itself, mean that an individual’s information was exfiltrated or, in the event it was, that the hackers exfiltrated every category of data itemised for each individual.’
Sackman said that there was nothing to indicate that the stolen data has been published or shared.
The LAA’s systems were breached in December 2024 – but the LAA only became aware of the cyber attack in April 2025. The LAA’s online portal was taken offline in May 2025 after the Ministry of Justice discovered that legal aid applicants’ personal data dating back to 2010 had been accessed. A few months later, the Ministry of Justice and LAA announced that the breach was bigger than they first thought.
This article is now closed for comment.
